name: 8-Bit Arcade
summary: A lost NES cartridge: strict 2C02 palette, black-outlined 3-colour sprites, tile-language meadows and checker-flicker ghosts.
description: Looks like it came from a forgotten NES/Famicom cartridge. Every colour comes from the NES PPU palette, every sprite has at most three colours plus a 1-px black outline, and the world is built from flat colour areas with hard tile-style edges: dark-green meadow with light-green lips, brown forest floor behind black cliff lines, ochre dirt roads, navy ponds, grey brick plazas with tombstones. There is no anti-aliasing, no gradient and no alpha anywhere in the world; transparency is a checkerboard and blinking is sprite flicker, so the screen reads like real 1986 hardware.
avoidFor: designs needing subtle lighting or many similar figure types

difficulty.why: New assets are small text grids (one char per pixel) with at most 3 colours plus an automatic black outline, and only 2 frames each; the strict NES palette and rules actually help, because there are fewer decisions to make. Variants are palette swaps of existing grids.

technique.resolution: 1 art pixel = 1.5 world units, so the 360-unit-tall view is a 240-row art buffer (NES height). Display scale up = max(1, round(screenH / 240)), buffer = ceil(screen / up), nearest-neighbour upscale. Ground chunks of 256 world units bake at 171 × 171 px.
technique.summary: All sprites are text grids (one char per pixel) mapped to NES colours by a builder that adds a 1-px black outline automatically; the ground is a material map evaluated on a 2×2-pixel block grid with tile-language edge rules (lip, cliff, ring) and hashed decal glyphs. Everything is blitted at whole art pixels.
technique.linework: 1-px pure black #000000 outline around every sprite, generated from the 4-neighbourhood of filled pixels (8-neighbour for number digits). Ground boundaries are single 1-px lines: black between grass and forest/water/plaza, light-green #00A800 lip on grass, ochre lip on forest, dark-brown edge on roads, sand lip where road meets water.
technique.shading: Flat colour fills. Volume comes from one light and one dark accent per sprite (e.g. tree canopy: light #58D854 crescent upper-left, black arc lower-right) and checkerboard dithering of black for shade. No gradients, no blending.
technique.lighting: No light system. The world is evenly lit; the only 'lighting' is the lantern sprite blinking between gold #F8B800 and white glass at 4 Hz and white-hot burst cores.
technique.texture: No noise texture. Surfaces get NES tile decals instead: 2-row grass tufts on an 8-px grid, 3×3 flowers, 1–2 px red/ochre leaf litter and black twigs on forest floor, pebbles on roads, a 12 × 6 running-bond brick tile on plazas, 2-frame animated wave glyphs on water.

paletteRules: Only colours from the NES 2C02 master palette; no tints, no mixes, no alpha in the world.
Each sprite layer uses at most 3 colours plus the black outline (the main character's head and body share orange, yellow, green, blue as two stacked NES sprites).
Ground is roughly 50% #005800 green, 25% #503000 forest floor, 10% #AC7C00 road, the rest water/stone/decals.
Every creature family is a palette swap: same grid, different map (purple vs magenta root creatures, white+cyan ghosts).
Flash is a palette swap to white/red/pink, never a white overlay.
Pure black is reserved for outlines, cliff lines, shadows and UI windows.

typography.role: Everything: HUD labels, numbers, menus, cards
typography.css: font: 16px/1 'Press Start 2P', monospace; color: #fcfcfc; text-shadow: none; letter-spacing: 0; text-transform: uppercase;

world.summary: A top-down overworld made of five flat materials (grass, forest floor, road, water, stone plaza) classified on a 2×2-art-pixel block grid from noise fields, then outlined with NES tile edge rules and stamped with tiny decal glyphs. No noise texture; water waves animate with 2 frames.
layers: Material map per 2×2 px block: plaza (octagon rect) > water (warped noise < 0.335) > road (distance to two noise-curve roads < 11 units) > forest (warped noise > 0.555) > grass
Base fills: grass #005800, forest #503000, road #AC7C00, water #0000BC, plaza brick tile #7C7C7C/#BCBCBC/#000000

Edge pixels: grass lip #00A800, black cliff forest/grass, ochre forest lip vs road/water, dark-brown road edge, sand road lip vs water, black + blue ring around water, black + light-grey ring around plazas
Decals (never on edge pixels): grass tufts on 8-px grid, flowers on 19-px grid, leaf litter on 5-px grid and twigs on 17-px grid on forest, pebbles on 7-px grid on roads
Per frame: 2-frame wave glyphs (cyan or blue, 5×2 px) toggling at 2.2 Hz on water anchors

characters.summary: All figures are text grids through one outline builder. Main character: a 13 × 19 px grid (+1 px outline = 15 × 21, about 22 × 31 world units) — a 10-row pumpkin head (orange #E45C10 with yellow #F8D878 carved eyes and zig-zag mouth, green stem) over a 7-row blue #0078F8 overall body with green vine sleeves and 2-row legs. Creatures: 14 × 15 px purple (#940084 or #D800CC) root creatures with leafy tops, slit eyes and a cream checkered mouth; white #FCFCFC floating ghosts with cyan shading and a checkered, outline-free tail; a 22 × 27 px purple-and-ochre root giant with gold eyes, cracks and long arms.
rules: Every sprite is a text grid; the builder adds the 1-px black outline, never draw it by hand
Max 3 colours + black per sprite part; big round head on a small body (the main character's head is 10 of 19 rows)
Faces are 1–3 px black or yellow eyes and a checkered mouth row (k/c alternation) — readable at 1×
Exactly 2 animation frames per figure; facing = horizontal flip of the canvas
Feet anchor: sprite bottom row sits on the figure's world y, snapped to whole art pixels
Families differ by silhouette first, palette second; variants are palette swaps of one grid
Ethereal figures get a checker tail (rows from tailFrom keep every other pixel, no outline, parity flips per frame)
Flash = palette swap (white head, red body); blinking = skip drawing every other 2-frame window

props.summary: Outlined NES sprites standing on the ground, built with the same grid builder: circle-built round trees (24 × 28, green or 16% autumn ochre/yellow) and bushes (18 × 10), grey dead trees (22 × 30), small rocks, orange pumpkins (11 × 8), ochre fences (16 × 9) and signposts, white tombstones and a stone pumpkin statue (14 × 22) on brick plazas.
rules: Same rules as figures: 1-px black outline, max 3 colours + black, flat fills, feet anchor on whole art pixels, y-sorted with the figures
Tree and bush canopies are overlapping circles: black lower-right rim (dd > 0.72 && nx + ny > 0.45), light upper-left crescent, global checker shade over the lower right
Trees: #00A800 canopy with #58D854 highlight (autumn: #AC7C00 with #F8D878) over a dark-red #881400 trunk with a black right edge
Every tree has a see-through checker copy (checker: 0) drawn when a figure stands behind it
Stone props (rocks, dead trees, tombstones, statue) use white/light grey on the upper left and mid grey on the right; tombstones carry a black cross
Wood props (fences, signposts) are ochre #AC7C00 with dark-brown #503000 rails and lines
Only trees (20 px), dead trees (12 px) and the statue (16 px) cast checker shadows

effects.name: Disappear burst
effects.how: 4 procedural frames on a (ceil(18R)|1)² grid, no outline: white core + gold cross, white/gold disc with red diagonal rays, red/gold checker ring, 8 flying bits. R = 1, 1.7 for the large creature. Each frame lasts 1/4 of 1 s.

effects.name: Appear puff
effects.how: 3 frames of white/light-grey circle blobs on a 17 × 15 grid (outlined), last frame 7 small grey dots in a ring without outline; 0.2 s per frame.

effects.name: Checker transparency
effects.how: Ghost tails and the main character's afterimages drop every other pixel ((x + y + parity) & 1); parity flips every 2 frames so the tail shimmers like NES sprite multiplexing.

effects.name: Pixel particles
effects.how: Impact and burst debris are 1–2 px squares in the struck figure's own colours with gravity 160–220; they blink (skip odd frames) in their last 30% of life.

effects.name: Star sparkle
effects.how: 3-frame white/gold (cyan for small collectibles) plus-star: 3×3 plus, 5×5 star, 4 corner dots. Used when collecting, on a flash, and as a ring of 10 stars.

effects.name: Spinning collectibles and orbiting lantern
effects.how: Small collectibles are 5 × 6 px cyan/blue diamonds, large ones 7 × 8 px gold/orange, spinning through 4 frames whose width shrinks to a sliver; the orbiting lantern is a 9 × 10 px purple-capped cream lantern whose glass blinks gold/white at 4 Hz.

effects.name: Seed projectile
effects.how: 2×2 cream/white square (outlined to 4×4), alternating colour every frame, with a 1-px gold/cream dot 4 px behind and an orange dot 7 px behind.

effects.name: Floating numbers
effects.how: 3×5 bitmap digits with 1-px gap, white; highlighted numbers gold at 2× scale; 8-neighbour black outline; blink in the last 25% of life.

atmosphere.summary: No light system, no post-processing in the world: even flat light with highlights baked into sprites, checker-dithered black shadows locked to the screen grid, checkerboard transparency, flicker for blinking, and only faint display scanlines when the upscale is 3 or more.
rules: Shadows are black ellipses w × round(w/3) with only checker pixels set; two parities baked, the one matching (screenX + screenY) & 1 is used
Shadow sizes: 8 ghost, 12 main character / small creature / dead tree, 16 statue, 20 tree, 24 large creature; all shadows drawn before any sprite
Light is implied only by upper-left sprite highlights and blinking glows (lantern glass gold/white at 4 Hz, white burst cores)
Transparency is always a checkerboard, never alpha; fading = flicker (skip drawing when frameCounter & 2)
No vignette, no fog, no bloom, no colour grading
Display-only CRT hint when up >= 3: darken the last display row of every art row with rgba(0,0,0,0.16) — the only alpha in the style
Menus dim the world with a black checker dither, never a translucent overlay; the black HUD bar frames the top of the screen

ui.summary: A solid black NES status bar across the top: red uppercase labels (-LIFE-), a row of 8 × 7 px hearts at 3×, a big white clock with a red caption, a counter with a tiny creature icon, a segmented cyan/blue progress bar with a 4-px white frame. Menus and cards are black windows with double white borders and a blinking triangle cursor; overlay screens dim the world with a black checker dither.

motion: Exactly 2 frames for every walk cycle: main character at the base anim rate, small creatures at anim × 1.6, the large creature at anim × 1.2 (one dust puff per footfall).
Idle bob: 1 art pixel toggled at 1.8 Hz; ghosts hover 3–4 px above their shadow, toggling at 2 Hz.
Collectibles spin with the frame sequence 0,0,0,1,2,3 at 9 fps and bob 1 px at 2.5 Hz.
No easing and no sub-pixel motion: positions round to whole art pixels; CSS transitions are none and blinks use steps(1).
Blinking flicker: skip drawing when (frameCounter & 2); fading particles and numbers blink the same way.
Water waves and lanterns use 2-frame toggles (2.2 Hz and 4 Hz).
do: Encode every sprite as a text grid with a char→colour map and let the builder add the black outline.
Keep each sprite to 3 colours + black and choose all colours from the NES palette list.
Snap every blit to whole art pixels (Math.round of the screen position) and upscale with smoothing off.
Use checkerboard pixels for transparency and shadows, flicker for blinking.
Make new creatures by palette-swapping existing grids before drawing new ones.
Give ground boundaries a 1-px lip or black cliff line so areas read like NES tiles.
Use Press Start 2P at multiples of 8 px for all text, uppercase labels in red #F83800.
dont: No gradients, glows, blur, alpha fades or anti-aliased shapes in the world.
No colours outside the NES palette (no #333 greys, no pastel tints).
No outlines in a colour other than black, and no 2-px outlines.
No rotation or scaling of sprites — use extra frames or flips instead.
No more than 2 animation frames for ordinary figures.
No smooth tweened UI: no rounded corners, no drop-shadow blur, no transitions.
No noise textures on the ground — only flat fills plus small glyph decals.
performance: Cheap. All sprites (2 frames × 2 facings × palette variants, effect frames, shadows) are baked once at init into tiny canvases; floating numbers are cached per value. Ground chunks (171 × 171 px) are baked incrementally with a generator that samples the noise fields on an 8-px grid and bilinearly interpolates; per frame only drawImage blits, a handful of wave fillRects and an optional scanline pattern (only when the upscale is ≥ 3) are drawn.
